name: ESP32-WROOM-32E-N4
title: ESP32-WROOM-32E / WROOM-32UE: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Bluetooth LE module, dual-core LX6, 4 to 16 MB flash
summary: A surface-mount radio module on the ESP32-D0WD-V3 chip: two Xtensa LX6 cores up to 240 MHz, 802.11b/g/n Wi-Fi, Bluetooth 4.2 BR/EDR and Bluetooth LE, with a 40 MHz crystal, quad-SPI flash and RF matching under a shield. The 32E (18 × 25.5 × 3.1 mm) has an etched antenna; the 32UE (18 × 19.2 × 3.2 mm) has a U.FL-type connector. 38 castellated pads bring out 26 GPIOs and the module runs from 3.0 to 3.6 V. ESP32-WROOM-32E-N4 is the 4 MB, no-PSRAM, -40 to 85 °C version.
key_figures: ESP32-D0WD-V3 (ESP32-D0WDR2-V3 in R2 variants), dual-core Xtensa LX6, 80 to 240 MHz

circuits.title: Typical application: supply, enable delay, reset, boot, UART, JTAG and 32 kHz crystal
circuits.description: The module on a base board with its support parts. The 3.3 V rail reaches 3V3 with 22 µF and 0.1 µF to ground. EN has an RC start-up delay (R1 up to the rail, C3 down to ground; values chosen by the designer, 10 kΩ and 1 µF being the usual pair) and a reset push button SW1, bridged by 0.1 µF, that pulls EN low through a 0 Ω link. A two-pin jumper ties IO0 to ground for download mode. A four-pin UART header carries VDD33, TXD0, RXD0 and ground; a four-pin JTAG header brings out TMS, TDI, TCK and TDO on IO14, IO12, IO13 and IO15. A 10 kΩ pull-up on IO16 serves the variants with in-package PSRAM. An optional 32.768 kHz crystal with 12 pF loads and a 5 MΩ to 10 MΩ parallel resistor can join IO32/IO33 through 0 Ω links; none of it is fitted by default. All ground pads, the exposed pad included, go to ground; the remaining GPIOs are left free.

operation.text: The module carries an ESP32-D0WD-V3 (or ESP32-D0WDR2-V3 with 2 MB in-package PSRAM on the R2 variants), a 40 MHz ±10 ppm crystal, a quad-SPI flash on chip GPIO6 to GPIO11 powered from VDD_SDIO, the RF matching network and either a PCB antenna (32E) or a U.FL-type connector (32UE), under a shield. Decoupling on the 3.3 V rail includes 10 µF, 1 µF, 0.1 µF and 100 pF; VDD_SDIO has 1 µF; a 2.0 nH inductor feeds the analogue supply. EN has an ESD diode, and U0TXD leaves the chip through 499 Ω. The crystal load capacitors and some matching parts depend on the crystal and board.

Two Xtensa LX6 32-bit cores, each controllable on its own, clocked from 80 MHz to 240 MHz, with 448 KB ROM, 520 KB SRAM and 16 KB RTC SRAM. A low-power coprocessor can watch peripherals while the main cores are off. Flash is 4, 8 or 16 MB; R2 variants add 2 MB PSRAM inside the chip package.

Wi-Fi 802.11b/g/n on 2412 to 2484 MHz, up to 150 Mbps on 802.11n, with A-MPDU and A-MSDU aggregation and 0.4 µs guard interval. Bluetooth 4.2 BR/EDR and Bluetooth LE, class 1, 2 and 3 transmit, AFH, CVSD and SBC. Certified for BQB; REACH and RoHS compliant. Reliability tests: HTOL, HTSL, uHAST, TCT and ESD.

Five pins are sampled at power-up or reset: GPIO0 and GPIO2 set the boot mode, MTDI (IO12) the VDD_SDIO voltage, MTDO (IO15) the boot-log output on U0TXD and, with GPIO5, the SDIO slave timing. Latches hold the sampled values until power-down; afterwards the pins work as ordinary I/O. eFuse bits EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE, EFUSE_SDIO_TIEH and EFUSE_DISABLE_JTAG also take part; they ship at 0 and, being one-time programmable, cannot return to 0 once set.

GPIO0 high boots from SPI flash whatever GPIO2 is. GPIO0 and GPIO2 both low enter joint download mode, which accepts firmware over UART or SDIO. Setting uart_download_dis to 1 removes download mode for good (chip revision v3.0 and later).

With MTDI low (the default) VDD_SDIO is fed straight from VDD3P3_RTC, normally 3.3 V; with MTDI high it comes from the internal 1.8 V LDO. If EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE is 1, EFUSE_SDIO_TIEH chooses instead: 0 selects the 1.8 V LDO and 1 selects VDD3P3_RTC.
Programming EFUSE_DISABLE_JTAG to 1 disables the JTAG signal source.

After the supply is applied the rails need at least 50 µs (tSTBL) to settle before CHIP_PU (the EN pad) goes high. Holding CHIP_PU below VIL_nRST (0.6 V) for at least 50 µs (tRST) resets the chip. An RC delay on EN is advised, usually 10 kΩ and 1 µF, tuned to the board's supply ramp and the reset timing.

34 GPIOs on the chip, 26 on the module pads. Four SPI controllers: SPI0 and SPI1 serve memory on GPIO6 to GPIO11, HSPI is on GPIO2, GPIO4 and GPIO12 to GPIO15, VSPI on GPIO5, GPIO18, GPIO19 and GPIO21 to GPIO23. Three UARTs up to 5 MBaud with hardware and software flow control, RS485 and IrDA. Two I2C controllers (100 kbit/s, 400 kbit/s, up to 5 MHz depending on pull-up strength, 7- and 10-bit addressing). I2S with PDM, an eight-channel RMT for infrared, eight 16-bit pulse counters, a sixteen-channel LED PWM with 20-bit resolution, and a motor-control PWM with three timers, six outputs, dead time, fault inputs and three capture channels. An SD/SDIO/MMC host up to 80 MHz in 1-, 4- and 8-bit modes for two cards; an SDIO/SPI slave up to 50 MHz. TWAI (CAN 2.0, ISO 11898-1) from 12.5 kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s on chip revision v3.x. A 10/100 Ethernet MAC that needs an external PHY over MII (17 signals) or RMII (9 signals), with IEEE 1588 PTP and 25/50 MHz clock output. Most functions can be routed to any GPIO through the GPIO matrix.

Two 12-bit SAR ADCs over 18 channels; the ULP coprocessor can sample in sleep and wake the CPU on a threshold. Two 8-bit DACs on GPIO25 and GPIO26, referenced to the supply. Ten capacitive touch inputs.

The connector is the first-generation type, mating with Hirose U.FL, I-PEX MHF I and Amphenol AMC plugs. No antenna ships with the module. Certification used a first-generation monopole, material code TFPD05H08750011. A suitable antenna is 2.4 GHz, 50 Ω, with peak gain no more than 2.33 dBi; another type or higher gain may need further testing such as EMC.
ESP32-WROOM-32E has an antenna keep-out zone at the antenna end of the module; ESP32-WROOM-32UE has none. The land pattern has thermal vias under the exposed pad.
Keep the module away from ultrasonic welding and cleaning: the vibration can make the internal crystal resonate and fail.
